opportunities.title: Corteva Open Innovation - rolling proposals in Digital Solutions / Plant Breeding (drone & satellite analytics, crop growth modeling, AI for breeding)
opportunities.program: Corteva Open Innovation (corporate agri-input company; sponsored/collaborative research)
opportunities.deadline_text: Traits, Plant Breeding, Enabling Technologies and Digital Solutions: evaluated on a rolling basis. Crop Protection and Biologicals: evaluated quarterly with cutoffs on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1.
opportunities.funding_text: "Typical collaborative and sponsored research projects funded through Open Innovation may receive up to $50,000 funding" to reach a defined proof of concept "within a one-year timeframe". "We may cover a maximum of 10% indirect costs for a project with academic and nonprofit research institutions only." Corteva also offers "Short term funding to support proposed research in areas of interest" and "Enabling Capabilities" (in-kind access to technology).
opportunities.duration: Proof of concept within a one-year timeframe
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Academics, research institutes, nonprofits, startups; students/postdocs with advisor support. FAQ refers to 'academic and nonprofit research institutions' for indirect-cost rules.
opportunities.eligible_countries: No country restriction stated on the official pages.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: No restriction on institution type or country is stated; CIAT/Alliance as a nonprofit research institution could submit directly as lead (indirect costs capped at 10%). Main issue is contractual: agreement terms (IP, confidentiality, publication) are negotiated case by case and must be compatible with CGIAR IP Principles/open-access policy - check with Alliance legal before pitching.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Not specified (submitter; advisor statement needed if student/postdoc).
opportunities.eligible_activities: Areas of interest include Plant Breeding: "crop growth modeling", "artificial intelligence application for breeding programs"; Digital Solutions: "improved analytics of drone and satellite imaging data for plant health diagnostics"; Enabling Technologies: "sensor platforms for in-field continuous characterization of soil composition and microclimates"; also crop protection, traits, biologicals.
opportunities.required_documents: Non-confidential proposal, "typically 1-3 pages in length", using Corteva's Collaboration Proposal Template.
opportunities.application_procedure: Submit via the Open Innovation site (links to Halo platform) either to a time-limited challenge or in an area of interest; Corteva responds with level of interest within 60 days; if selected, virtual pitch/Q&A, then funding level, resources and agreement terms are agreed.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Digital Solutions (drone/satellite analytics for plant health) and Plant Breeding (crop growth modeling, AI for breeding) match the researcher's UAV/hyperspectral phenotyping, deep learning and crop modelling skills directly; focus is industry R&D proof-of-concept rather than smallholder climate adaptation.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Small, short corporate grant; useful for a seed-company partnership and phenotyping pipeline demonstration (e.g., maize/rice in LAC) but limited for sustaining multi-year staff; IP/confidentiality terms may conflict with CGIAR open-access.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: A 1-3 page proposal on UAV/satellite-based plant health or phenotype prediction is fully within existing capabilities.
opportunities.recommendation: Corporate open-innovation funding. Pursue opportunistically: submit a 1-3 page non-confidential proposal under Digital Solutions or Plant Breeding (e.g., UAV/hyperspectral + DL phenotyping for disease/stress in maize trials, or crop-model-assisted GxE prediction). Low effort, rolling, but expect max ~USD 50k / 12 months and negotiate IP terms early.
opportunities.potential_partners: Corteva/Pioneer breeding stations in Colombia/Mexico/Brazil; CIMMYT (maize)
opportunities.next_action: Draft a 1-3 page non-confidential concept using the Collaboration Proposal Template; confirm with Alliance legal/BD that a sponsored-research agreement with Corteva fits CGIAR IP principles; submit via openinnovation.corteva.com (questions: openinnovation@corteva.com).

evidence.deadline_quote: Areas of interest page: Traits, Plant Breeding, Enabling Technologies and Digital Solutions are "evaluated on a rolling basis"; FAQ: "we aim to respond with our level of interest within 60 days of receiving your proposal."
evidence.eligibility_quote: "We may cover a maximum of 10% indirect costs for a project with academic and nonprofit research institutions only."
evidence.status_quote: "Short term funding to support proposed research in areas of interest." / Digital Solutions: "improved analytics of drone and satellite imaging data for plant health diagnostics"
evidence.staff_costs_quote: Not specified - FAQ only states "Depending on the project, we may provide in kind resources"; process page says funding levels are agreed case by case.

opportunities.title: World Coffee Research (WCR) - Innovea Global Coffee Breeding Network / member-funded research partnerships (partnership-based, no open call)
opportunities.funder: World Coffee Research (industry-funded by 200+ coffee companies incl. Starbucks, Tchibo, Keurig Dr Pepper; co-funders incl. JDE Peet's, Lavazza Foundation, Taylors of Harrogate)
opportunities.program: Corporate-funded industry research consortium (Innovea breeding network; CafeClima; molecular breeding tools initiative)
opportunities.deadline_text: No call; partnership-based. No requests for proposals found on worldcoffeeresearch.org (checked 2026-10-22).
opportunities.funding_text: Example: USD 1.5 million initiative (5 June 2026) funded by an FFAR grant "matched by industry co-investment from Taylors of Harrogate, Coffee Circle, and other WCR member companies"; Uganda seed-systems effort where UNIDO, JDE Peet's, The J.M. Smucker Co. and Lavazza Foundation "commit EUR 850,000 toward a WCR-led effort".
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Not applicable - WCR selects national research partners (e.g., Cenicafe, KALRO, USDA-ARS) and technical collaborators.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Coffee-producing countries in the WCR network (Colombia via Cenicafe among others).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: The Alliance already partners with WCR: CafeClima (Feb 2026) uses advanced climate projections supplied by the Alliance (Eric Rahn quoted). Route is a sub-award/partnership, not a competitive application.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Breeding (Innovea network), molecular markers, variety trials, climate suitability tools (CafeClima).
opportunities.application_procedure: No public procedure; partnership negotiated with WCR.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Multi-location variety trials + climate modelling are a natural fit for UAV/RS phenotyping, ML and crop/climate suitability modelling; the June 2026 initiative itself is genomics-focused and does not fund phenotyping.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Existing Alliance-WCR relationship (CafeClima), Colombia/LAC coffee focus, corporate co-funding pipeline (FFAR + member companies).
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: High-throughput phenotyping of Innovea trials and climate-informed variety recommendations are within team capabilities.
opportunities.recommendation: Strategic monitoring (corporate-funded consortium): propose a remote-sensing/UAV phenotyping + climate-modelling add-on to WCR's Innovea trials (incl. Cenicafe), building on CafeClima. Funding would likely come from WCR member companies or FFAR-matched grants.
opportunities.potential_partners: WCR, Cenicafe (FNC Colombia), Taylors of Harrogate, Coffee Circle, Alliance coffee team (Eric Rahn)
opportunities.next_action: Coordinate with Alliance coffee researchers (Eric Rahn) and contact the WCR science team to explore a phenotyping/climate-analytics workstream for the Innovea network; watch WCR news for new co-funded initiatives.

opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate-risk analytics, EO monitoring/MRV for landscapes and coffee suitability modelling are relevant, but the facility is primarily finance.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Colombia coffee landscapes, climate resilience, private-capital mobilization; complements Alliance coffee/climate work.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance has coffee climate-suitability models and EO capacity for landscape monitoring.

opportunities.title: AWS Open Data Sponsorship Program (free S3 storage + egress for open, cloud-optimized datasets)
opportunities.program: Registry of Open Data on AWS - Open Data Sponsorship Program (corporate in-kind)
opportunities.deadline_text: "We evaluate applications on a rolling basis." Decisions generally communicated "within a two-week period."
opportunities.funding_text: Program "covers the cost of storing and sharing publicly available, high-value, cloud-optimized datasets"; FAQ: "The program covers Amazon S3 storage costs for the specific dataset approved under the program" plus distribution costs (egress, cross-region). Compute/analytics not covered.
opportunities.duration: Not specified on loaded official pages (periodic renewal review described)
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Data providers with openly licensed, well-documented datasets; signer must be an authorized representative of the organization.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: No applicant-type restriction stated; the Alliance can apply directly as data provider. Constraint: "Datasets must be accessible to all users, usable for any purpose, and available at no cost" (CC BY 4.0 recommended; NC/ND licences excluded).
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Authorized representative of the data-providing organization.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Hosting and distribution of open, cloud-optimized datasets (e.g., COG/Zarr crop-yield forecasts, climate projections, EO-derived maps) on the Registry of Open Data.
opportunities.required_documents: Online application: contacts, institution, dataset name/description, size, growth rate, formats, license, intended use and novelty.
opportunities.application_procedure: Review Terms and Conditions, submit the form at application.opendata.aws; rolling review.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Supports climate data infrastructure / open dissemination of RS and crop-model outputs; does not fund research itself.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Free, durable hosting for Alliance open datasets (e.g., Climate Data Hub layers) increases reuse and visibility; no staff funding.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team already produces COG/NetCDF/Zarr datasets with metadata.
opportunities.recommendation: Apply for one flagship open dataset (e.g., gridded crop yield forecasts or downscaled climate/crop-suitability layers already CC BY 4.0) to remove storage/egress costs.
opportunities.next_action: Pick a CC BY 4.0 dataset, convert to cloud-optimized formats, read the T&Cs and submit at application.opendata.aws.

opportunities.title: Google TPU Research Cloud (TRC) - free Cloud TPU access for researchers
opportunities.deadline_text: "Invitations are sent out to approved applicants on a rolling basis."
opportunities.funding_text: "TRC enables researchers to access a cluster of more than 1,000 Cloud TPU devices"; accepted researchers "will have access to Cloud TPUs at no charge." "While Cloud TPUs are free to use for TRC participants, other GCP services are not."
opportunities.duration: Quota granted "on a temporary basis"; length not specified
opportunities.eligible_applicants: "Anyone can express interest in joining the program by signing up."
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Individual researchers express interest; no institutional restriction stated. Obligation to share results openly (papers, open-source code, blog posts) fits CGIAR open-access policy.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Researcher; agree to Google Terms, Privacy Policy and AI principles; share feedback with Google.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Training/inference of ML models on Cloud TPUs (TensorFlow, PyTorch, JAX, Julia) - e.g., EO foundation-model fine-tuning, crop-type/phenology deep learning.
opportunities.application_procedure: Submit the 'Express interest' form; rolling invitations.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Directly useful for deep learning / geospatial foundation-model work on Sentinel/Landsat time series.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Compute only; no staff funding; complements existing Google Cloud/Earth Engine credits in the dashboard.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team uses TensorFlow; JAX/PyTorch-XLA porting may be needed for best TPU use.
opportunities.recommendation: Low-effort add-on: express interest for a specific EO deep-learning project (e.g., rice phenology/crop mapping foundation-model fine-tuning). Budget small GCP costs for VMs/storage.
opportunities.next_action: Submit the TRC express-interest form describing an EO/agriculture DL project and planned open outputs.
